newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam orders changes at top of oil and gas firm.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam orders changes at top of oil and gas firm.

text.p: Vietnam has ordered far-reaching changes in the boardroom of its oil and gas firm, Petrovietnam, including the replacement of Ho Si Thoang as president and chief executive officer, sources at the company said on Monday.
The sources told Reuters that Thoang, who had led state-owned Petrovietnam through a period of rapid expansion in Vietnam's oil and gas industry, would be replaced by Ngo Thuong San from October 1.
San is Director of VietSovPetro, a Vietnamese-Russian joint venture which is the country's biggest oil producer.

Tran Canh, formerly director of the company's exploration and production arm PVEP, will become vice-president for development and production and Nguyen Xuan Nham will become vice-president of services.
The sources said Thoang, although no longer president or a member of the board of directors, would become chairman of Petrovietnam's currently six-member management board.
There was no official confirmation of the boardroom changes and the sources declined to give a reason.
Western oil industry executives said the reshuffle could reflect government frustration over hitches which have marred the image of Vietnam's oil business as an emerging energy frontier in East Asia.

Earlier this year the Royal Dutch/Shell Group allowed a production-sharing contract off Vietnam's coast to expire after taking what it described as "a more realistic view" of operating in the country.

Petrovietnam has also run into problems with the Australian firm Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, which has said it would be interested in any reasonable offer for its stake in the Dai Hung oil project, another offshore Vietnamese field.

BHP, which fully wrote down its A$151 million Dai Hung investment in its 1995/96 accounts, had been trying to renegotiate terms of its contract with Petrovietnam after estimates of the field's reserves were slashed.
